clue.text: Unyielding, like an enterprise led by Napoleon?

definitions.text: like an enterprise led by Napoleon?
definitions.meaning: Napoleon is the boar who rules the farm in Orwell's Animal Farm, so his enterprise has a pig at its head

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the answer literally: headed by a pig. Napoleon is not the French emperor here but the pig leader in George Orwell's novel Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinate and stubborn is described as unyielding.

clue.text: Resentment as card game has wasted time

indicators.note: has wasted means the time letter is lost from the game

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two players

explanation.surface: A card player grows resentful because the game has dragged on.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritation from wounded pride is a kind of resentment.

clue.text: Wry expression, but I am in favour

indicators.note: in puts the contraction inside the word for favour

parts.note: grace means favour, as in being in someone's good graces
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face while insisting they are in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted face showing disgust or pain is a wry look.

clue.text: Loving running away from work in small group

indicators.note: in puts the work inside the small group

parts.note: an element is a small group within a larger body, as in a rowdy element
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone in love flees from their job in a small team.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to marry are doing that.

clue.text: Line up one's friends in part of the house

parts.note: in military drill, to dress ranks is to line them up
a circle is one's group of friends

explanation.surface: Someone arranges their friends in a row in a room of their home.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is a theatre, and the answer is the first balcony above the stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: The first gallery in a theatre auditorium is a section of the seating.

clue.text: Ready without delay to turn up for medic

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: COD, cash on delivery, means paying ready money at once

explanation.surface: A doctor is ready to arrive at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is money (readies), and cash on delivery is payment with no delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor is a medic.

clue.text: Problem unpoetic passage presented right to the end

indicators.note: presented here means the letter for right is delivered or handed along to a new place
to the end says where that letter finishes up: at the very back of the word

parts.note: prose is writing that is not verse, so a passage of it is unpoetic

explanation.surface: Someone is told an unpoetic passage was moved to the end of a reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presented ... to the end' moves the R of PROSE from second place to the back, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or knotty difficulty is a problem.

clue.text: These coppers are the start of police getting expanded

definitions.text: These coppers are the start of police getting expanded

parts.words: These coppers are the start of police getting expanded
parts.note: the first letter of police is the abbreviation for small copper coins, and writing that abbreviation out in full gives their name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' are not policemen but bronze coins; the letter P written out in full is their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper coins in Britain are small units of money, a hundred to the pound.

clue.text: To keep quiet about success is very difficult

indicators.note: about means the call for quiet goes round the other words

parts.note: sh is what you say to tell someone to keep quiet
a win is a success
taken as written

explanation.surface: Staying silent about one's achievements is very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is only a link. The answer is used informally for something horribly hard, as in 'a swine of a job'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty and hard to do can be called a swine, hence brutish.

clue.text: He had several brushes with night-watchmen

definitions.text: He had several brushes with night-watchmen

parts.words: He had several brushes with night-watchmen
parts.note: brushes are paintbrushes, and the night-watchmen are the militia in the Dutch master's famous painting The Night Watch

explanation.walkthrough: Brushes suggest skirmishes with guards, but the painter used his brushes on The Night Watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch painter of The Night Watch is the man meant.

clue.text: Don's quiet finally disturbed-beast's waded back in

indicators.note: a beast that has waded in has entered the water, signalling one piece going inside another
in places the turned-round beast inside the reworked word
the final letter of the word is disturbed, shifted out of its last place

parts.note: taken as written, the word quiet

indicators.note: back means the word for the beast is turned round

parts.note: an ox is a beast of the field; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A college don's peace was finally broken when an animal waded back into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally disturbed' shifts the last letter one place, making QUITE, and 'back' turns the beast round; 'waded ... in' then slots it inside. 'Don' is the Spanish title, not a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes's knight is Don Quixote, so this is the Don's surname.

clue.text: Businesses split by new sanction

indicators.note: split by means the two business words are parted, with something placed between them

parts.note: CO is short for company, one business
a firm is another business

explanation.surface: Companies are being broken up because of a newly imposed sanction.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Businesses', supplies both companies, and 'split by' wedges the abbreviation for new between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction a decision is to ratify or approve it formally.

clue.text: Cancel periods last in timetable

parts.note: eras are long periods of history

indicators.note: last in picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A clerk scraps the final periods of the day on a school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete or wipe out something is to cancel it.

clue.text: Graves he provides are situated between two rivers

indicators.note: between puts the word for being situated in the middle of the two rivers

parts.note: the Somme is a river in northern France
R is the map abbreviation for river
to lie somewhere is to be situated there

explanation.surface: Someone digs graves and places them in a valley between two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graves' is not burial plots but Graves, a Bordeaux wine; one phrase, 'two rivers', gives both SOMME and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter serves bottles such as Graves to diners.

clue.text: Some wet dew sprinkled around a plant

indicators.note: around means the scattered letters wrap round the single letter
sprinkled means the letters are scattered about like drops

explanation.surface: Morning dew is scattered over a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprinkled' rearranges SOME WET DEW, and 'around' puts that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy-flowered wild herb of damp meadows is the plant meant.

clue.text: Explosive love contained — it could turn the bed over

definitions.text: it could turn the bed over

indicators.note: contained means the zero for love is held within the explosive

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bomb blast was held in check before it could wreck a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, and turning it over means working the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardening tool with a blade is used to dig and break up soil in a flower bed.

clue.text: Skilful work, installing two taps on small boat

parts.note: taps are marked H and C, for hot and cold
a raft is a small simple boat

explanation.surface: A craftsman fits a pair of taps on a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps are labelled H and C, read as 'H and C'; that goes before RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made skilfully by hand is craftsmanship.

clue.text: Ecstasy to laze in bath, perhaps, for an old Englishman

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Ecstasy is lying idle in a hot bath, a pleasure for an old Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges LAZE IN BATH into LIZABETHAN, which follows E. The answer means someone of the reign of Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of Queen Elizabeth I's sixteenth-century reign was an English person of long ago.

clue.text: Plant's name in, say, botanical language and English

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

indicators.note: in puts the name letter inside the language

parts.note: plants are named scientifically in Latin

explanation.surface: A plant's name is given in botanical Latin and in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant's' reads as 'Plant is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbriar, a wild rose, is a plant.

clue.text: If you study here long enough, will it dawn on you?

definitions.text: If you study here long enough, will it dawn on you?

parts.words: If you study here long enough, will it dawn on you?
parts.note: evening classes run after dark, so a student who stays very late would see the dawn break; dawn on also means become clear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn on you' means both 'become clear to you' and literally the sunrise reaching you after studying all night.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult evening classes run in the dark hours after work.

clue.text: Part of body, about a pound weight, he'll devour

indicators.note: about means the gut goes round the pound letter

parts.note: the gut is part of the body
L is the symbol for a pound
a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: Someone who gains a pound in one body part will eat anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater is someone who will eat everything.

clue.text: Put some snap into a piece of drill

definitions.meaning: past tense of bite: snapped the teeth into something
the cutting attachment fitted into a drill

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap into' is to bite, and its past tense is the answer; a drill also takes interchangeable cutting pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting tip in a drill and the past of biting share one spelling.

clue.text: Sue's to live at address with no parking

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: with no means the parking letter is taken away

parts.note: a speech is an address
P is the symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Someone sues to live at an address where there is no parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue's' reads as 'Sue is'; sue here is to plead or petition, not to take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition or plead is to sue.

clue.text: Legion left in care of noblewoman

indicators.note: in the care of means held safely by, so the left letter goes inside the noblewoman

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman, wife of an earl

explanation.surface: A Roman legion was left in the keeping of a titled lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' looks like a noun for an army but is an adjective meaning very many.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are legion are innumerable, too many to number.

clue.text: Time for music

parts.note: the speed at which a piece of music is to be played

explanation.definitionFit: The pace of a musical piece is its time.

clue.text: Fitting groups in shelters

definitions.meaning: sets of tables or boxes that fit one inside another
the homes birds build to shelter their young

explanation.walkthrough: A nest of tables is a set that slots together, hence 'fitting groups'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds' homes and sets of tables that slot together share the same name.

clue.text: Delighted to get round cold trail

indicators.note: to get round means the delighted word encircles the cold letter

parts.note: sent means thrilled, delighted

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to pick up a cold trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound follows the smell left by a quarry, its trail.

clue.text: Note tucked into weapon is for divine hunter

indicators.note: tucked into means the note is slipped inside the weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical note is stuffed into a gun belonging to a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of the hunt was a deity who pursued game.

clue.text: Mark's escort

definitions.meaning: to notice or observe, as in mark my words
to accompany, as in ... someone home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' reads as 'Mark is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice and to accompany someone home share the same short verb.

clue.text: Looking ill, but translating Livy with pronounced ease

indicators.note: translating turns one text into another form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the name of the Roman historian

indicators.note: pronounced means the word ease counts for its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: spoken aloud, the word ease sounds like E's: more than one letter E

explanation.surface: A schoolboy looks sick while translating the Roman historian Livy, which he claims to do with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced ease' sounds like E's, a plural of the letter E, supplying three of them; 'translating' rearranges LIVY with EEE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent glance believed to cause harm is an ill-wishing look.

clue.text: Measure in which two people proverbially co-operate

definitions.text: Measure in which two people proverbially co-operate

parts.words: Measure in which two people proverbially co-operate
parts.note: a measure is a dance, and the proverb says it takes two to do this Argentine one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' is an old word for a dance; the proverb is 'it takes two to' dance this one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argentine ballroom dance is the subject of the saying about needing two people.

clue.text: One keeps crossing oneself, taking such a bold leap

definitions.text: One keeps crossing oneself, taking such a bold leap

parts.words: One keeps crossing oneself, taking such a bold leap
parts.note: a ballet dancer jumps and repeatedly crosses the legs in the air, not making a religious sign

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing oneself' suggests a religious gesture, but the dancer crosses the feet over and over mid-jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet jump in which the dancer beats the calves together several times is that leap.
